# Nothing left out: the audit of step 2.105

Area 2 of [LEADS.md](../LEADS.md). Written by the area lead on 2026-11-14, against commit `4360f77` of the build branch.

**The question.** Every promise the specification makes must be built, be in a plan, or be named for a later stage with a reason. This file says where each promise is, and lists the ones that are nowhere.

**What was read.** Every file in `docs/specs/v1/`: the nine product files, the ten technical files, `README.md`, `PROGRESS.md`, `LEGAL-BRIEF.md` and `DECISIONS.md` (its opening sections, the "Decided for you" table, the change log and the product rows line by line; its technical rows were compared with the technical files by ID, since they repeat them). Against: `docs/build/STAGE-1.md`, `STAGE-2.md`, `STATUS.md`, `STAGE-1-REPORT.md`, the build order (T10), and the code.

**What was not done, so nobody assumes it.**

- The open lanes (2.33, 2.45, 2.85, 2.93, 2.107) were not read. Where a finding may already be answered inside one of them, it says so.
- No screen was opened in a browser. That is the job of the "using it" audit (step 2.106). Here "built" means the code and its tests are in the repository, not that a person has used it.
- Step 2.105's own done test asks for a second sub-agent to pick twenty promises at random and confirm them. That has not been run. Every row below names a file or a step so that it can be.
- Nothing in the product, the plans or the specification was changed.

**The previous attempt.** It left a folder of twelve files, one per spec file, each holding a heading and an empty table: no rows had been written. Its status words were sound and are kept here, a little simplified. The folder is removed; this one file replaces it.

## 1. In short

Section 5 holds 594 rows, one for each promise or group of promises, across the 23 files. Counted by the status each row carries:

| Built | Part built | Planned | Later | Later, T10 silent | Founder | Rule kept | Half | Nowhere | Dropped | Total |
| ----- | ---------- | ------- | ----- | ----------------- | ------- | --------- | ---- | ------- | ------- | ----- |
| 101   | 97         | 46      | 142   | 33                | 25      | 40        | 49   | 60      | 1       | 594   |

So 451 rows are built, planned, kept by a check, the founder's, or named for a later stage. 142 are not: 60 are nowhere, 49 are half done with the rest in no step, and 33 belong to a later stage whose list in the build order does not name them. Many of those rows are the same gap seen from several files (export alone is nine rows), so the 142 rows come down to the 34 findings of section 2.

The specification holds up well against the plans for the part of the product a season runs on: the schedule, results, standings, statistics, the tracker and the league fence each have a step for every promise, and most are built. What is missing sits around the edges of that core, in three places:

1. **Getting a league and a person in and out.** There is no way to make or publish a league except the made-up seed, no way for a signed-in person to find their league, and nothing for handing over, exporting or deleting. These were each somebody else's step, so they were nobody's.
2. **Settings that are promised but have no home.** Who sees players' names, the league's own words, roster limits, the coin flip.
3. **The later stages' lists in the build order.** T10 names a stage's big pieces and leaves out about forty smaller promises the product files make. Nothing is wrong yet, because stages 3 to 6 have no plan yet; these are the things that will be lost when those plans are written from T10.

Three findings are High, seventeen Medium and fourteen Low. Section 6 proposes 22 steps or changes to steps.

## 2. Findings

Severity as in LEADS.md. **High:** a person is stopped, misled or put at risk, or the product cannot go online. **Medium:** must be fixed before real people use it. **Low:** tidying. "Spec" gives the file and line; "Plan" and "Code" say what was looked for and not found.

### High

**H1. A league cannot be made, published or renamed on a real database.**

- Spec: T10 line 31, "Leagues created by an internal tool"; P3 line 116, "We create each league ourselves using an internal version of the same four steps"; P2 line 128 and DECISIONS line 41 (U-9, decided for you), "The owner publishes, archives and un-archives."
- Plan: `STAGE-1-REPORT.md` line 21 lists "Creating a league (internal tool)" as existing. No step in either plan makes a tool or a screen for it. Step 2.48's settings screen shows declared settings only; step 2.60 says "renaming the league … is a setting", but no screen sets a league's name.
- Code: the commands exist (`packages/core/src/modules/leagues/commands/create-league.ts`, `set-league-status.ts`, `set-league-name.ts`, `rename-short-name.ts`, `create-season.ts`, `set-current-season.ts`). The only caller of any of them is the seed (`packages/database/src/seed/seed-leagues.ts` lines 148 to 153). Nothing in `apps/` or `scripts/` calls them.
- Why it is High: the demo milestone (T10 line 53) needs the demo league to exist on the platform, the Al-Hadi transfer (`scripts/transfer-tracker-games.mjs`) and the Faraj transfer (step 2.79) both need a league and a season to run into, and the founder's supervised session can show only the two made-up seed leagues. After steps 2.92 to 2.97 land, the product can go online and still nobody can put a league on it.
- Proposed step 1.

**H2. Who sees players' names has no setting, no screen and no step, and real children's names are next.**

- Spec: P6 line 116 (R-14: a youth league starts at first name and last initial, "The league's admin can switch to full names and photos, confirming that the league has the permission it needs"); P6 line 117 (R-15); P6 line 119 (R-17: "a person can ask for their name to be taken off a league's public pages"); P4 line 94 (League settings → Privacy); T4 line 92 (T-81: "one league-level switch the admin controls", and the person's own request in `people.visibility`).
- Plan: step 2.11 built the one function that applies the policy. No step declares the league's switch, sets a person's request, or puts either on a screen. Step 2.14's settings are the start page, who may score and the two statistics settings only.
- Code: the policy reaches the public pages from one place, the stand-in: `apps/web/src/server/stand-in-public-stats.ts` lines 543 and 544 (`namePolicy: defaultNamePolicy`). `packages/core/src/modules/leagues/settings/declarations.ts` declares four settings, none about names. No command in `packages/core/src/modules/people/commands` writes `visibility`.
- Why it is High: step 2.93 is open now and moves the public pages onto the database, where there is nowhere to read this from, so its builder must invent one. And the demo league is a youth league with real students (P9 line 124): the school's answer about names (LEGAL-BRIEF line 25) cannot be acted on in either direction, and a parent's request to take a name down could only be met by editing the database.
- Proposed step 2.

**H3. A signed-in person has nowhere to go.**

- Spec: P2 line 67 ("Signed in: your leagues first"); P2 line 71 (`/account`: "the leagues you belong to"); P2 line 124 (U-8: "the account button at the top right … or 'Sign in'" on every page of every league); P2 line 141 ("The front page and the account button list them all").
- Plan: T10 line 100 puts "Our own front page" in stage 5. Step 2.102 gives the front page and the account pages a look and says "What each page does … stay the same". No step gives them anything to do.
- Code: after signing in a person is sent to `/account` unless a page asked for them back (`apps/web/src/server/sign-in/flows.ts` line 49). `/account` lists devices and two sign-out buttons, nothing else (`apps/web/src/app/(platform)/account/page.tsx`, 49 lines). `/` is `<NotBuilt title="page.home" />`: "This page is not built yet." A league's header shows "Sign in" to a visitor and nothing at all to a signed-in person (`apps/web/src/features/shell/site-header.tsx` lines 37 to 41), and its "Sign in" link carries no way back to the league.
- Why it is High: at the demo milestone Al-Hadi's coach and scorekeepers get real accounts (T10 line 53). One who taps "Sign in" on the league's page ends on a list of devices with no link to the league, to the admin or to their games. This is a person stopped, on game night.
- Proposed step 3. The "using it" audit (2.106) will see the same thing from the screen side; this is the promise it comes from.

### Low

**L1. Whether a league is listed (U-10) cannot be changed after it is made.** P2 line 130; P9 line 138 ("renaming and listing the league is a setting"). `listed` is set once in `create-league.ts` line 49. Step 2.60 builds the notice and "do not index" only. Fold into step 2.60 or proposed step 1.

**L2. Names and numbers edited at the scorer's table.** P7 line 29 ("Jersey numbers … can be changed at the scorer's table"). The current tracker has a Players panel for it (`apps/live-stats/public/js/roster-editor.js`). Step 2.35's line has "add a player on the spot" only. For the live-scoring audit (2.107) to place.

**L3. No font is served.** T5 line 34: "Fonts come from a fixed list we host ourselves." `packages/site/src/design/fonts.ts` names seven; no font file or `@font-face` is in the repository at this commit, so every design falls back to the device's fonts. Step 2.85 may be answering this in its lane; its review should check.

**L4. `sessions.tidy` has no step.** T7 line 37. The sign-in store of migration 0012 (codes, attempt counts, sessions) is never cleaned. Fold into step 2.91, which gives the worker its first nightly timer.

**L5. The spec contradicts itself about clubs.** P2 line 163 (U-12, agreed): "programs and clubs exist in the database from the start". T3 lines 90 and 116: club scopes are refused "until the `clubs` table exists". Correct one of them in step 2.100.

**L6. The states every screen must handle are not in the page-step checks.** T9 line 57 (T-184: "nothing here yet, loading, an error, no permission, and (where relevant) offline"); P4 line 73 (A-4: a failed save "says so and keeps what was typed"). `STAGE-2.md` line 18 lists five checks for a page step; these are not among them.

**L7. Help.** P4 line 85 (A-10: "a '?' that opens the relevant help article") and T9 line 135 (T-200: help articles "written with the feature … not afterwards") against T10 line 100, which puts help articles in stage 5. Page steps add "short help text" only. Either T-200 or T10 should change.

**L8. The checks a person does by hand.** T9 line 74 ("a manual pass by keyboard and with a screen reader before release"); T9 line 87 (Safari and Firefox). The browser tests run in Chromium and Edge only, and neither hand check is on the founder's lists or in step 2.63's checklist.

**L9. Housekeeping the spec promises.** T9 line 100 ("A short list of known shortcuts lives in `docs/`": there is none); T9 line 98 (T-192: a fifth of each stage for tidying: no step in stage 2).

**L10. Retiring what the new product replaces.** T1 lines 151 to 153 (T-15): the tracker's own server, `apps/varsity-preview` and `apps/varsity-hosted` are "retired and removed after Al-Hadi's move". No step at the end of stage 2 does it or says when.

**L11. Things the spec puts off that T10's last list does not carry.** T10 line 124 against: S-14 referees (P7 line 79 says stage 6; P7 line 202 says later), S-15, S-19, S-20, text messages and "live now" alerts (P8 line 112), a league's own sending domain (P8 line 108), a league's own code (P5 line 13), sharing a design (P5 line 36), club pages (P5 line 142), eligibility records (P9 line 106), build-your-own roles (P4 line 50).

**L12. How we know it is working.** P1 lines 99 to 106 set six measures; nothing records any of them. T4 line 95 promises cookieless page counts; no stage names them.

**L13. Small things with no owner.** Overtime "shown on the result" (P7 line 164): no mark in the game card. The import template to download and matching columns by hand (P3 line 78): step 2.59 says the seed's files "double as the templates", and no screen offers one. Entering a past season's final standings and champions without its games (P3 line 79), which also runs against A-12. The Faraj-like seed league of T-195 (T9 line 107): step 2.59 builds the demo-shaped one only. "Creation times" (T3 line 222) and where a level final score is "reported to the admin" (T3 line 153) are left open in the spec itself.

**L14. A sport is not yet a "sport definition".** P1 line 80 and T5 lines 141 to 144: a sport is declared with its periods, statistics and standings defaults. Today a program carries a `sport_key` and the basketball lists live where each step needed them. Nothing is wrong for basketball; the day a second sport is wanted (after stage 6) this is the work. Worth one line in T10.

| Stage 2 or 3  | The player's page (M6); page titles and share images (M7); the league's own words as a function (M12)                                         | P2 83; P5 136; T5 129            |
| Stage 3       | Uploads: the `assets` table, Supabase Storage, images decoded and re-encoded, logos for league, season and team                               | T3 162; T4 80; P5 32, 134        |

| Stage 3       | Export, as a row of the Faraj acceptance table (M1)                                                                                           | P9 45                            |
| Stage 3       | The features switches and our own rollout flags                                                                                               | P4 91; T5 134 to 137             |

## 5. Every promise, file by file

One table for each file of the specification. "Line" is the line in that file at commit `4360f77`. A row is one promise, or one decision with the promises that hang together under it.

The status words:

- **Built**: the code and its tests are in the repository and its step is ticked.
- **Part built**: some of it is built and a named step finishes it.
- **Planned**: a step that is not ticked yet.
- **Later**: T10 names it in a later stage.
- **Later, T10 silent**: the spec puts it later, and T10's list for that stage does not name it (section 4).
- **Founder**: only the founder can do it. The row says whether it is on a founder list.
- **Rule kept**: a rule about how we work or build, kept by a check, a test or the runbook.
- **Half**: part is built and the rest is in no step.
- **Nowhere**: in no code, no step and no stage.
- **Dropped**: the spec itself dropped it.

## 6. Proposed steps

For the lead to number and add, or to write in the log why not. Each says who it is for, what that person sees or does when it is done, what it needs, and its done test. Steps 1 to 3 answer the High findings and should open ahead of new features (LEADS.md, section 5). Where a step needs a product answer that is not settled, it says so: the lead decides it and marks it "Decided for you".

**1. Making, naming and publishing a league.** _Answers H1, L1._

- Who for: the founder and the lead, who must put the demo league and Faraj's on the platform; and a league's owner.
- What they see or do: (a) one command on this computer, an "internal version of the four steps" (P3 line 116), that takes a league's name, short name, sport, who plays, city, time zone, contact email and the owner's email, and makes the league in draft with its first season, on whichever database it is pointed at by the migration login's settings. It prints what it will do and asks before doing it. (b) League settings → Profile: the owner or an admin changes the name, the short name (told that the old address forwards for 12 months), the contact email, city and time zone, and whether the league is listed. (c) A Publish button, and Archive and Un-archive, as U-9 was decided (DECISIONS line 41).
- Needs: 2.93 (the website on the database), 2.97 (so the owner can be invited). Part (a) needs nothing new.
- Done test: on PGlite, the tool makes a draft league for an email that has no account yet; that person signs up and is its owner. In a browser: the owner opens the draft league, a visitor gets "not found", the owner renames it and publishes, the visitor now sees it, and the old address forwards. Each change is in the activity log; a scheduler is refused; isolation and role cases for anything new.
- To decide: whether an admin, or only the owner, may publish (the spec gives admins "the same access" bar three things, so: admins may).

**2. Who sees players' names.** _Answers H2._

- Who for: a youth league's admin, and a parent or player who asks for a name to come down.
- What they see or do: League settings → Privacy, drawn from declared settings like every other (T-98): "Names on public pages" (full names; first name and last initial, the start for youth and mixed leagues; switching to full names asks the admin to confirm the league has the permission it needs, R-14), and "Players may ask to appear as initials" (off to start, R-15). On a person's record in People: "Show as" (as the league shows everyone, initials, or removed), set by an admin or registrar, with the reason kept in the activity log.
- Needs: 2.14, 2.17; lands before or with the stats and team parts of 2.93, which read it.
- Done test: the T-81 scan passes under each setting; in a browser the admin switches to full names and the team page changes, a person set to "removed" shows as a nameless line whose numbers still add up (R-17), and a scorekeeper cannot reach the setting.

**3. A signed-in person can find their way.** _Answers H3._

- Who for: everyone with an account, first of all Al-Hadi's coach and scorekeepers.
- What they see or do: on every league page an account button at the top right: "Sign in" for a visitor; for a signed-in person their name or initials, opening a small menu with "Admin" (if they have an admin area here), "My games to score" (if a scorekeeper), "Your account" and "Sign out". Signing in from a league page brings them back to that page. `/account` lists the leagues they belong to with their role in each, each a link. `/` shows a signed-in person the same list first, and a visitor one plain page: what SR Leagues is and "Sign in". Nothing more of stage 5's front page is built here.
- Needs: 2.85 (the header), 2.93 for real leagues. Step 2.102 should follow it, not precede it.
- Done test: browser tests at phone width: an invited scorekeeper taps "Sign in" on the league home, signs in, is back on the league home, and reaches their games in two taps; from `/` they see their league; a member of two leagues sees both; a visitor sees no league that is in draft.

On `/account`: change the name, change the password (asks the old one, signs out other devices, emails the account), change the email (a code to the new address, a notice to the old one, T-73).

**5. The admin's home.** _Answers M4._

- Who for: an owner or admin opening the admin on a phone.
- What they see or do: "To do", each line a button to the task: games past their start with no result, schedule changes not published, walk-up players to review, postponed games with no new date. "Today and next": today's games with status and scorekeeper, or the next game day. "This season": teams, games played of total. "Recent activity": the last ten log lines. A season picker at the top of every admin screen, and a search box that finds a person, team or game by name. Roles see only the lines they can act on.
- Needs: 2.27, 2.53, 2.71, 2.77; can land in parts as those do.
- Done test: with the demo-shaped seed league, each kind of to-do appears and its button lands on the right screen; an empty league says so in plain words; a scheduler sees no people lines.

**6. Starting a new season.** _Answers M5._

- What they see or do: "Start a new season": a name and dates, copied rules and settings from the last one, and one choice: bring the teams (and, if wanted, their rosters) or start fresh. Carried teams keep their line through the seasons. "Make this the current season", and "Archive" for the old one, which stays under the season picker and can no longer be changed except by a correction.
- Needs: 2.15, 2.18, 2.19, 2.47.
- Done test: a season is started from the last with teams carried; the public season picker shows both; a result cannot be entered in an archived season without a reopening; isolation and role cases.

It follows the team's statistics setting and the name settings; a youth league's player pages ask not to be indexed (T4 line 94); a league can switch player pages off. Names on the team and statistics pages link to it.
- Needs: 2.40, 2.44, 2.46, proposed step 2.

**8. Exporting everything (O-9).** _Answers M1._

- Who for: a league's owner or admin.

The worker builds one download of spreadsheet files (teams, people, rosters, games, statistics, standings, settings; later registrations and site content as they exist). They are told when it is ready; the link works for 24 hours and only for them; the export is in the activity log. Cells that could be read as formulas are made safe.
